:::{#def-bias-variance-tradeoff}
#### Bias--variance trade-off

Let $\candproc{1}, \ldots, \candproc{\ncand}$ be [fitting procedures](#def-fitting-procedure),
each [at least as flexible](#def-flexibility) as the one before,
and let $\trainset$ be a random [training set](#def-training-set).
At a covariate value $\predvar$,
with $\targetfn$ the [mean function](#def-mean-function),
there is a **bias--variance trade-off** among them
when, from each procedure to the next,
the squared [bias](#def-prediction-bias)
of the prediction, used as an [estimator](estimation.qmd#def-estimator) of $\targetfnf{\predvar}$, does not rise
and its [variance](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/variance-covariance.html#def-variance)
does not fall:

$$
\ba
\sqf{\bias{\candproc{\icand + 1}\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}} &\le \sqf{\bias{\candproc{\icand}\paren{\predvar; \trainset}}},
\\
\Var{\candproc{\icand + 1}\paren{\predvar; \trainset}} &\ge \Var{\candproc{\icand}\paren{\predvar; \trainset}},
\qquad \icand = 1, \ldots, \ncand - 1.
\ea
$$ {#eq-bias-variance-tradeoff}

Source: @james2021islr2e [sec. 2.2.2].

:::
